Poco Book has no dedicated value objects for guardian contact details.
The add-student feature needs validated guardian values before parser,
storage, and UI integration.

Add immutable guardian name and phone objects with normalized storage.
Preserve name capitalization for display and ignore case in equality,
with consistent hashing. Require eight phone digits starting with 6, 8,
or 9, and remove spaces and hyphens before storage.

Follow the submitted MVP rules and error messages so later integration
can rely on one validation contract. Cover invalid inputs, boundaries,
normalization, Unicode case variants, and equality with unit tests.

Validation: ./gradlew check passes all 252 tests and Checkstyle.

Refs: #25

commitResults.messageTitle: Add students with guardian contact and optional fee
commitResults.messageBody:
The add command still required AB3's phone, email and address, and
had no way to record a guardian or an outstanding fee, so tutors could
not record a student as specified in Feature 1 of the MVP spec.

Let's require n/, g/ and gp/, make p/, e/, a/ and f/ optional, and
validate every field with the spec's rules and exact messages.
Duplicates are now the same name, ignoring case and extra spaces, with
the same guardian phone. Guardian details and the fee are saved and
loaded so they survive a restart.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep the selected student's details current
commitResults.messageBody:
Editing the viewed student with edit or setoutstanding cleared the
details pane, although the User Guide says the selection stays while
the student is still displayed. The list panel looked for the old
Person, which an edit replaces.

The list panel now records in-place replacements and restores the
edited student. The details pane also shows the fee as S$AMOUNT, as
the cards and command results do.

commitResults.messageTitle: Align edit output with the User Guide
commitResults.messageBody:
edit reported an invalid index as "The person index provided is
invalid." instead of the student message the User Guide specifies,
and still used AB3's "person" wording. Command results also no
longer listed tags, so a successful tag edit showed no change.

edit also absorbed g/, gp/ and f/ into the preceding value, so
"edit 1 a/123 Street g/New Guardian" saved that text as the address.
These fields cannot be edited, so edit now rejects them with the
invalid-command-format message.

commitResults.messageTitle: Allow prefix-like text in add addresses
commitResults.messageBody:
add rejected addresses such as "c/o Mr Lim" or "Blk A/B" as unknown
prefixes, although Address allows '/' and edit accepts them. Only
values other than the address are now checked for unknown prefixes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Accept find keywords that have no letters
commitResults.messageBody:
find validated each keyword as a full name, which needs a letter, so
"find Alex 2" failed although "Alex 2" is a valid name. Keywords are
now checked against the name characters only, and are normalized to
NFC like stored names.

list, find, fees, help and exit saved the address book. If the data
file failed to load, any of them overwrote it with an empty book.
Like view, they no longer save.

Also replace list's AB3 "Listed all persons." with "Listed all
students.".

commitResults.messageTitle: Report oversized setoutstanding index as invalid
commitResults.messageBody:
An index above 2147483647 gave an invalid-command-format message,
unlike delete, edit and view, which report "The student index
provided is invalid.". setoutstanding now uses the same index parsing.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject null entries in the data file
commitResults.messageBody:
A null entry in the persons list caused an uncaught
NullPointerException on startup. It is now reported as invalid data,
so the app starts with an empty address book as for other invalid
files.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update the guides for the v1.3 fixes
commitResults.messageBody:
The Quick Start and manual-testing add examples omitted the required
g/ and gp/ parameters, so pasting them failed. Update them, and
document the behaviour changed by the preceding fixes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject null tag entries in the data file
commitResults.messageBody:
A null entry in a student's tags list caused an uncaught
NullPointerException on startup. Report it as an invalid tag so the app
starts with an empty address book as for other invalid files.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show guardian contact details on student cards
commitResults.messageBody:
Student cards omitted guardian name and phone, so two students with the
same name and no optional student contact details appeared identical in
the list, contradicting UC02 extension 2b.

Display each student's guardian name and phone on their card.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update version, help URL, and guide details
commitResults.messageBody:
Point HelpWindow.USERGUIDE_URL to the Poco Book User Guide, bump
MainApp.VERSION to V1.3.0, add exit to the User Guide command summary,
and document guardian card labels under list.

commitResults.messageTitle: Start edit and delete details on a new line
commitResults.messageBody:
Messages.format returns a multi-line student summary starting with
"Name: ...". AddCommand separates its header from this block with a
newline, whereas EditCommand and DeleteCommand placed "Name: ..." on
the same line as "Edited student:" or "Deleted student:".

Place a newline after "Edited student:" and "Deleted student:" so all
formatted student fields align consistently on their own lines.

commitResults.messageTitle: Match default window width to minimum width
commitResults.messageBody:
MainWindow.fxml and the Developer Guide specify a minimum window width
of 750 px, whereas GuiSettings.DEFAULT_WIDTH was still 740 px.

Update GuiSettings.DEFAULT_WIDTH to 750 so fresh launches and saved
default preferences match the minimum window width.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject broken external symlinks in runtime paths
commitResults.messageBody:
ApplicationPaths.resolveWithin called Path.toRealPath() on existing
directory entries without following links first. When a runtime path
component was a dangling symbolic link, toRealPath() threw
NoSuchFileException and wrapped it in IllegalStateException instead of
checking whether the link target stayed inside the home folder. In
addition, MainApp resolved its runtime paths in static field
initializers, so an invalid link caused ExceptionInInitializerError
whenever MainApp was loaded.

Inspect symbolic link targets when the destination does not exist yet so
broken links escaping the home folder raise IllegalArgumentException,
and defer MainApp runtime path resolution to init().

commitResults.messageTitle: Allow edit command to update guardian details
commitResults.messageBody:
EditCommand and EditCommandParser reject the guardian name (g/) and
guardian phone (gp/) prefixes, so tutors cannot update guardian contact
details without deleting and re-adding a student.

Allow users to update a student's guardian name and guardian phone
through the edit command while keeping untouched fields and duplicate
student identity checks intact.

Closes #107

commitResults.messageTitle: Add logging to EditCommand and EditCommandParser
commitResults.messageBody:
EditCommand and EditCommandParser lack feature-level diagnostic logs
for parsed edit descriptors and completed student updates.

Log parsed edit descriptors at FINE in EditCommandParser and successful
student edits at INFO in EditCommand using LogsCenter.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document guardian edit in Developer Guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The Developer Guide does not yet describe how the edit command updates
guardian details or verifies student identity after an edit.

Add an Implementation section and sequence diagram explaining how
EditCommandParser and EditCommand update guardian fields while
preserving untouched fields and checking duplicate student identity.

commitResults.messageTitle: Expand guardian edit tests and builder support
commitResults.messageBody:
EditCommand.MESSAGE_USAGE omits a guardian prefix in its example, and
EditPersonDescriptorBuilder does not support guardian fields directly,
requiring manual setter calls in tests. Test coverage also combines
single-field guardian edits and lacks dedicated checks for shared
guardian phones, gp/-only identity collisions, and filtered persistence.

Include gp/ in EditCommand's usage example and add guardian support to
EditPersonDescriptorBuilder and PersonUtil. Split the single-field
guardian edit tests and add regression tests for shared guardian phones,
gp/-only duplicate identity checks, and filtered edits persisted through
LogicManager and JsonAddressBookStorage.

commitResults.messageBody:
Find matching rules and index resolution after a find had little
test coverage, so later MVP changes could break them unnoticed.

Let's add FindCommandTest cases for single, multiple, case-insensitive,
partial-word, zero-match and result-order behaviour, plus an
integration test showing that delete after find uses the index in the
filtered list.

No production change is needed; current behaviour meets the spec.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use student wording in find and delete messages
commitResults.messageBody:
The app manages students, but find and delete still reported results
in terms of 'persons', which does not match the product or issue #3's
requirement that find states the number of students listed.

Let's update the result, error and usage messages for find and delete,
and reuse the existing student index error message (as view does).
Constant names are kept so existing references stay valid.

commitResults.messageTitle: Decouple find integration test from index error wording
commitResults.messageBody:
PR #67 changes delete's invalid-index error from the person message to
the student message. Asserting the exact text here would make this test
fail whichever of the two PRs merges second.

Let's assert only the exception type and that no data changed, leaving
the exact error text to DeleteCommandTest.
Use student wording in find and delete messages

commitResults.messageTitle: Show guardian and fee details in delete success message
commitResults.messageBody: The delete success message only shows the original AB3 fields, so tutors cannot see the guardian contact or outstanding fee of the student they just removed.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject find keywords that cannot appear in a name
commitResults.messageBody:
find accepts any keyword, so `find @@@` succeeds with an empty list
and clears what the tutor was looking at, although no student name
can ever contain such a word. It also has no test that guardian
names are excluded from the search.

Let's reject keywords that fail the existing name rule, keeping the
displayed list unchanged, and add a test that a keyword matching
only the guardian name finds nothing.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use S$ for fees in student details and test delete after fees
commitResults.messageBody:
The delete success message shows fees with a `$` prefix, while the
MVP spec, the student card and the fee commands all use `S$`. Also,
#2 requires delete to use the index of the list shown by `fees`, but
nothing tested this because `fees` was not merged yet.

Let's use `S$` in the formatted student details, and add a test that
deletes the third student in the `fees` list, which is a different
student from the third one in the full list.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document find keyword rules and drop redundant comment
commitResults.messageBody:
The user guide does not say that find rejects keywords which cannot
appear in a name, or that guardian, contact and fee details are not
searched. The comment above the keyword check also just repeats what
the code says.

Let's add both points to the find section of the user guide and
remove the comment.
Show guardian and fee details in delete success message
Reject find keywords that cannot appear in a name

Tutors need to find a student when they only remember the guardian's
name or phone number.

Match any keyword against whole guardian-name words, ignoring case, or
against the exact stored 8-digit guardian phone.

commitResults.messageTitle: Match guardian phone keywords typed with separators
commitResults.messageBody:
add and edit accept gp/9234-5678 and store 92345678, so a tutor
searching the way they typed it found nobody.

Normalize phone-shaped keywords with GuardianPhone before comparing.
Also copy the keyword list, reject null arguments, add hashCode and
document the constructor, with tests for compound names, numeric name
words and the defensive copy.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add findguardian command to search by guardian name or phone
commitResults.messageBody:
Tutors often remember a guardian's name or number from a message
rather than the student's name, but find only searches student names.

Add FindGuardianCommand and its parser. Keywords use the guardian-name
character rules, search all stored students regardless of the current
filter, and leave stored data unchanged.

Command registration and user guide text are left to the shared
integration PR, as agreed in #98.

commitResults.messageTitle: Harden findguardian parser and command from review
commitResults.messageBody:
Reject null arguments in the command and parser, mark parse with
@Override, fix its Javadoc tags, and say in the usage text which phone
numbers are matched.

Add tests that go through the parser for a hyphenated phone and for
siblings sharing a guardian, checking each sibling is listed once in
stored order even after a prior filter.

commitResults.messageBody:
Student records do not retain guardian contacts or optional fees through
application restarts, preventing dependent features from relying on stored
data.

Let's extend the model and JSON adapter with validated guardian and fee
fields. Add round-trip and invalid-data coverage so normalized phones, fee
boundaries, absent fees, ordering, and duplicate behavior remain stable.

Person now hashes guardian and outstanding-fee fields, but the updated
hashCode path is not exercised.

Let's verify equal records produce the same hash code so the equality
contract remains covered as fields evolve.
Make absent outstanding fees explicit through Optional and update callers to handle them safely. Use realistic sample fees and clarify why edit tests preserve fields that edit cannot change.

The fees command lists every student with an outstanding fee, so tutors
cannot focus the list on students owing at least a chosen amount.

Add an optional min/AMOUNT threshold while preserving plain fees and the
existing result-count message. Keep the query read-only and reject invalid
arguments without changing the displayed list or stored records.

Cover amount boundaries, strict parsing, search replacement, displayed
indexes, fee clearing, and the storage boundary with fees-specific tests.

Implements #119.

commitResults.messageTitle: Address minimum fee filtering review feedback
commitResults.messageBody:
Numeric threshold equality lacks a matching hash code, and the live
filter tests only cover clearing a fee entirely.

Normalize threshold hashes and test positive fees crossing the minimum
to protect value equality and inclusive live filtering. Reuse the shared
amount regex and plain-fee predicate to avoid duplicated definitions.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add logging for minimum fee filtering
commitResults.messageBody:
Fee filtering lacks feature-level diagnostics for successful queries
and rejected arguments.

Log the threshold and result count at INFO and parser diagnostics at
FINE using LogsCenter, consistent with existing logging conventions.
Avoid including student records in these messages.

Direct command callers can supply negative thresholds, and command
diagnostics omit the minimum amount.

Reject negative constructor inputs, describe thresholds with
ToStringBuilder, and make the parser null precondition explicit.
Add regression tests and rename the integration test to describe its
inclusive filtering and no-save guarantees.

Explain the minimum-fee query so future developers can follow its
parsing, live filtering and no-save behavior. Add a sequence diagram
and its rendered image beside the implementation explanation.

Relates to #100; documents the implementation in #137.

Fix selection moving to different student
commitResults.messageBody:
A search that showed the same number of students as before moved the
selection and the details pane to whichever student was then at the
same index (#132). PersonListPanel paired rows of the displayed list
by position, but a search reports that list as replaced in full.

Record replaced students from the full student list instead, which a
search does not change, and add Logic#getPersonList() to provide it.
This also keeps a renamed student selected after they stop matching
the current search.

A command that fails after changing data, such as when saving the
data file fails, could also leave a different student selected, or
none. Correct the selection after a failed command if it moved, and
leave it untouched otherwise, so a typing mistake does not scroll the
list.

commitResults.messageTitle: Block non-answer keys in delete dialog
commitResults.messageBody:
The dialog ignores keys other than Y, N and Esc but lets them pass
on, so they could still reach a keyboard shortcut in the dialog.
Block every key except Esc, which the Cancel button handles.

Also test that Y confirms a student who owes a fee, and that the
second check refuses a student whose details change during
confirmation.
